# BH00010 (Unnamed)

*Translated on 17 Qudrat 183 using GPT 6.1 Sol*

**1** In the name of our Lord, the Most Holy, the Most Great, the Most Exalted, the All-Glorious.

**2** Praise be to God, who is peerless in love and unique in affection. He is indeed the Lord of all servants, the Master of creation, who speaks whatever He wills in the beginning and the return. May the fragrance wafting from the garment of God, the light shining from the horizon of His loving care, and the peace manifest and radiant from the kingdom of His grace rest upon those who have arisen to exalt His Word and make His Cause manifest, and have acted as they were commanded in His Book. These are servants through whom the commandments and laws have gained currency among humanity and the rule of sanctity has been established among its peoples. Through them the banners have been raised and the signs have appeared. The Concourse on high will surely bless them, and beyond them, the Lord of Names and Creator of heaven.

**3** To continue: from the horizon of the heaven of your affection there has shone forth that which has stirred the winds of love. It is indeed a letter in which the vessel of your innate nature has overflowed. When I perceived its fragrance and recognized your condition in the Cause of God, my Lord and your Lord and the Lord of all who are in the heavens and on earth, I set out for the praised station where the throne of the Lord of existence, the Sovereign of the unseen and the seen, is established. I entered His presence and presented what the nightingale of your sincerity had sung upon the branch of faithfulness. Then the face of the Lord of Names turned toward me. By God, He spoke words that made the mountains take flight, yet nothing was imprinted upon the mirror of my heart except in the measure of my affliction, lowliness, poverty, and need. O beloved of my heart, how can a drop encompass the ocean of utterance? By the life of my Beloved and yours, I speak only the truth. I tell you truly, and that Beloved of the heart bears witness and testimony, for through the grace of God He has been and remains aware.

**4** He said—exalted be His grandeur and great His majesty:

**5** In the name of the Wronged One of the world.

**6** O ʿAlī, praise be to God, the sight of the world is illumined by the kohl of the wisdom and utterance of the loved ones of God. Although the dark clouds of the people’s vain imaginings have prevented this light from appearing and becoming manifest, the winds of His will shall assuredly disperse these clouds. He is powerful and mighty, and His power, though concealed today, is secretly engaged in conquering the cities of hearts. The utterance of the All-Merciful is a mighty key that unlocks, a sun shining and radiant, and an all-encompassing ocean. It unlocks, sheds light, and bestows life. Blessed is the discerning one whom doubt and uncertainty, vain imaginings and conjectures, and the power and wrath of the people of the world have not kept from the loftiest summit. Through one word the world is thrown into turmoil, and through another it becomes still and assured; through one deed it is set ablaze, and through another it becomes coolness and peace. Thus, in the scriptures and tablets, the Most Exalted Pen has numbered spiritual character, pleasing deeds, and a good word among the mighty hosts of God. Beyond all these considerations, if people hold fast to fairness, they themselves will attain the lights of certitude and behold the signs, proofs, and testimonies of God—exalted be His glory—as clearly as the sun, and the throne of God’s power will also be seen, manifest and resplendent, amidst the world.

**7** O Akbar, convey greetings of praise to the friends and tell them on behalf of the Wronged One: You must be distinguished from the other people of the world and at all times keep distinction in view. Know your own worth and recognize the station of the loved ones of God who have arisen to serve from the beginning of the Cause. The Most Exalted Pen has mentioned everyone and adorned them with robes of loving care, yet from the tablets of steadfast, unwavering souls the fragrance of distinction is diffused. Blessed is the one who has perceived it and is among those who act.

**8** O you who look toward God, I testify that you drank the choice wine of My love in the earliest days of My revelation, acknowledged what God acknowledged, held fast to it, spread His writings, and stood ready to serve Him on a day when feet faltered. Convey greetings of praise on My behalf to My loved ones in Ṭāʾ and those around it, and give them the glad tidings of the loving care of God, the Lord of the worlds.

**9** We counsel them to observe pure godliness and to do whatever exalts the Cause of God, the All-Knowing, the All-Aware. Say: Have mercy on yourselves, on the Tree of the Cause, and on the blood shed to exalt the Word of God, which all must obey. Fear God, O people, and be fair-minded. Do not squander your deeds and what you have endured for this mighty Announcement. You may well take pride before all who dwell on earth, for you have attained what no one else in creation has attained. To this bears witness He whose mention the Mother Book has voiced, the Almighty, the Wondrous. Do not make yourselves the playthings of the ignorant of the earth. Every deed attributed to you should shine like the sun amidst the world. Thus God admonishes you with true admonition, as a mercy from Him. He loves you and desires for you what befits your stations before God, the Most Exalted, the Most Great. Beware of doing anything that would hold back mercy in the heaven of His will. Thus counsels you One who is more compassionate toward you than you are toward yourselves. Your Lord, the All-Merciful, is indeed the All-Knowing, the All-Wise. May the glory shining from the horizon of My loving care and the light gleaming from the heaven of My mercy rest upon you and upon those who are with you and love you in the path of God, the Lord of this blessed and manifest Day. End.

**10** God willing, all the friends of God will be adorned with the garment of sanctity. They should conduct themselves in such a way that, were they to arise in the assembly of the world to admonish and counsel its people and speak with the utmost eloquence, they would neither be inwardly ashamed nor give anyone on earth grounds for objection. Now, night and day, they should devise ways to guide a soul and give it a taste of the choice wine of recognition. These are not days for divided thought, faltering will, impure intent, inconsistent deeds, or harsh character. All deeds, actions, and qualities should be seen as a single point; that is, the focus of them all should be known, so that they may point to the true Object of recognition and reflect Him. All have been and remain beneath the gaze of His loving care. There is no one who has not attained the crown of remembrance from God, the All-Protecting, the Self-Subsisting.

**11** Now the loved ones of God must hold fast to what is necessary. They will assuredly also witness days of ease, joy, and honor. He continually says that, if they recognize the Summoner and taste the sweetness of the All-Merciful’s utterance, they will count the world as nothing and direct their gaze toward whatever exalts the Cause, cleaving and holding fast to it.

**12** In any case, this servant conveys to each one greetings of peace and praise, in self-effacement and nothingness, and with the utmost helplessness and supplication begs these mines of the jewels of divine love to keep their lofty stations in view and act as befits them. The plea and the helplessness are this servant’s; acceptance rests with the loved ones of God, the Almighty, the Beloved.

**13** The mention you had made of the two devoted souls, the honored Āqā Siyyid Muḥammad and Ustād Muḥammad-Qulī—may the glory of God rest upon them both—and likewise of their work in the path of God, was presented in the most exalted, most holy, most inaccessible Court. For each of them the sun of loving care, the moon of tenderness, the star of compassion, and the exalted Word appeared and shone forth. His words—exalted and glorified be He:

**14** In My name, the Summoner in the world.

**15** O Muḥammad, you have been mentioned before the Wronged One time after time, and each time We have remembered you in words from which the sincere perceive the fragrance of My loving care. Rejoice and be among the thankful. At this moment We remember you once again as a bounty from Our presence. Your Lord is indeed the Almighty, the All-Bountiful.

**16** Praise God, for He has mentioned your work in the Tablets and sent down for you that which adorns you with the ornament of sincerity. He is indeed the All-Powerful, the Omnipotent. What you have done in My path has attained My good pleasure and the ornament of My acceptance. Your Lord is indeed the All-Knowing, the All-Wise.

**17** Blessed are you and your work, and whoever has acted as commanded in My clear Book. Through your arising to serve Me and your work out of love for Me, the Concourse on high has proclaimed: “Blessed is the one who has been faithful to the Covenant of God on this blessed and wondrous Day.” May the glory, shining, manifest, radiant, and resplendent, rest upon you and upon every steadfast servant.

**18** And this is what was sent down from the dominion of grace for the honored Ustād Muḥammad-Qulī, may the glory of God rest upon him. His words—exalted be His majesty:

**19** In My name, the Guardian over the outward and the inward.

**20** O Muḥammad-Qulī, the Wronged One remembers you from where He dwells, reminds you of His covenant, and sends down for you what you have done while holding fast to His Book. Blessed are you for having remained faithful and done what you were commanded out of love for Him. How many a servant has clung to the paths of delusion, turning away from His path, and how many a servant has cast the world behind him, turning toward the lights of His face! Rejoice that He has enabled you to do what draws you closer to Him in every circumstance. Happy are you for having turned to God and perceived the fragrance of His garment. We have remembered you before and afterward. Your Lord rewards whoever holds fast to the cord of His loving care. May the glory shining from the horizon of the heaven of grace rest upon you and upon whoever follows His command. End of quotation.

**21** Blessed and happy are they both, for, as God bears witness, the fragrance of sincerity wafts from them, and with joy and gladness they have done what they were commanded. God willing, may you preserve this most exalted station in the name of the True One, exalted be His glory. This servant, who is passing away, asks and hopes that the exalted True One will grant them supreme steadfastness. He has power over all things. Conveying greetings and salutations to them depends upon the will and kindness of that beloved friend.

**22** What you wrote concerning the honored leaf Ḥāʾ-Vāv, may the glory of God rest upon her, was presented. He said: “Excellent is the kindness shown to her.” God willing, may they be assisted in performing good deeds and whatever reflects pure wisdom. God willing, may the relatives receive the loving care of the True One and be adorned with supreme steadfastness, so that the clamors of calamity may not keep them from the path of divine unity.

**23** O ʿAlī-Akbar, upon you be My glory, My mercy, and My loving care. Consider, then speak of a woman who returned to her abode. She exchanged light for fire and sold the King of humanity for a piece of diamond. Despite all her love, devotion, and claims to recognition, the calamity deceived her with a diamond flower. She has turned away from the True One and toward another. Such is the condition of the world and its people. From the beginning of the Cause she has turned away and has never had, nor does she now have, any understanding, for she has not been with Us. The meaningless deference and humility of the gentlemen of Qāf induced those souls to profess belief. He knows what is within the breasts and what is within the hearts, and He is the All-Knowing, the All-Informed.

**24** If a single leaf among the leaves reflects upon her actions, deeds, and conduct, she will speak and say, “I am free of her and of everything she possesses,” and will shield her face from hers. You know that the Most Exalted Pen had refrained from mentioning those souls. Yet, in view of the oppression, transgression, and flame of selfish desire, these words have flowed and descended from the Most Exalted Pen, and this too is so that they may recognize her and become acquainted with her actions and deeds. May God protect us and you from her and others like her. End of quotation.

**25** This passing soul asks and hopes that the True One, exalted be His glory, will guide the friends in that land to the straight path of trustworthiness, integrity, truthfulness, and purity, so that all may rest at ease beneath the shelter of the True One and His loving care.

**26** On one occasion this exalted utterance was heard from the tongue of the Lord of Names. He said: “O servant who is present, everything has had and has an originating principle. The saying that ordinary people have repeated and still repeat, ‘Without leaven, dough remains unleavened,’ is entirely sound; it is the saying of a wise and discerning person. Today the companions of God are the leaven of the peoples of the world. All should draw upon their trustworthiness, truthfulness, steadfastness, deeds, and character. Ask the True One that they may perceive the fragrance of awareness and hold fast to what will elevate their standing and stations.” End of quotation.

**27** Some of the dissenters among the people of the Bayān have objected that, despite the claim to truth, His companions practice wickedness and indecency, whereas the companions of the Primal Point practice piety and are adorned with trustworthiness and integrity. This statement departs from the path of truth and honesty, for, as this servant knows, ever since the Ancient Beauty arrived in Iraq, verses and utterances were continually revealed and dispatched in the utmost secrecy, all enjoining what God willed and forbidding what He prohibited in the Book.

**28** Some time ago the Tongue of Grandeur spoke these exalted words: “From Iraq, the Land of Mystery, and the Land of the Prison, We continually counseled the people of the Bayān and commanded what befits the Cause of God. Still, rebellion and corruption have not ceased. Most remain defiled and have not attained purity and sanctity.” End of quotation.

**29** That beloved friend is himself aware of the atrocious deeds that appeared among this group. Truly, one cannot describe them. No one had control over his own wife, children, possessions, or property. Most were rebellious, insubordinate, and tyrannical, yet considered themselves among the sincere companions of God. A few were seen to be free of such conduct and suspicions, and that only at the beginning of the Cause. Afterward, you yourself witnessed what they did and what happened, to such an extent that the Most Exalted One—may the life of all else be sacrificed for Him—expressed astonishment. Outwardly, however, He said nothing, for there was no supporter or helper. In His last days He wrote a Tablet in which He complained most strongly of those souls and expressed dissatisfaction with the majority. It was, however, kept concealed, since wisdom did not permit its disclosure.

**30** People are weak. As was witnessed, despite the radiance of the Sun of Truth at high noon and the appearance of the Tree beyond which there is no passing on the right side of the White Spot, each person, following his own desire, presented a delusion in the guise of certainty. In any event, were we to discuss these matters, sheets and volumes would not suffice.

**31** In this Most Great Revelation, however, even the enemies have testified and continue to testify to purity, sanctity, loftiness, and exaltation. One of the divines of Yazd had said: “At the beginning of the turmoil, the deeds of this community were beyond description. Now they are seen gathering in assemblies, reciting verses and prayers, and displaying the utmost trustworthiness and integrity. Evidently this is at the command of the new leader.” Consider how many souls in this Revelation freely drank the cup of martyrdom, and how many sacrificed themselves by their own hands, although the True One did not approve. Even now there are souls who are pure, sanctified, and free from every fault. Our Lord, the All-Knowing, is indeed the Witness, the All-Informed.

**32** This servant will relate one account of trustworthiness and fidelity to a pledge, so that perhaps some may take heed and know with certainty that beneath His canopies God has servants possessed of great trustworthiness, good deeds, and spiritual qualities. In Alexandria, several of the friends of God were engaged in earning a livelihood in accordance with the command, and in this Most Great Revelation earning a livelihood has been accounted worship. We ask Him to enable everyone to fulfill what He has willed, and

**33** The account is this: the honored Āqā Shaykh ʿAlī, son of the honored Ḥājī ʿAbd al-Raḥīm, may the glory of God rest upon them both, went to Khartoum to keep company with the beloved of the heart, the honored Ḥājī Mīrzā Ḥaydar ʿAlī, and the spiritual friend, the honored Ḥāʾ and Sīn, may the glory of God rest upon them both. For the two imprisoned names had written requesting that one of the companions come to keep them company and inform them of events in the Land of Desire and its surroundings, as well as in Iran. The aforementioned Shaykh resolved to go and set out for the sake of God.

**34** For a time they were gathered like leaves on the trees of love, fresh and flourishing from the gentle air and the light, luminous water. Suddenly the autumn wind began to blow, and circumstances arose that brought about separation. The two aforementioned names, may the praise of God rest upon them both, turned toward this region and attained their desire, while the honored Shaykh remained in that land earning a livelihood.

**35** After a number of successive years, in accordance with the binding command, the honored Ḥājī ʿAbd Allāh, upon him be 669 \[the glory of God\], set out for that region to keep the honored Shaykh company, assist him in his worldly occupations, and help him return. Owing to the unsettled state of affairs, however, this was prolonged until the honored Shaykh, may the glory of God rest upon him, ascended. After his ascension, the aforementioned Ḥājī ʿAbd Allāh attended to the settling of his affairs.

**36** The Iranian consul in that city wrote an account of the deceased’s affairs, as well as his goods and property, to the chief agent of the Imperial Government of Iran, who resides in Cairo. The latter requested from the property and estate the fee prescribed by law. The two most exalted names, the honored Muḥammad and ʿAlī, may the glory of God rest upon them both, wrote from Alexandria that whatever was rightfully his would reach him. Some merchants of Cairo who had embraced the Cause told the aforementioned agent, “This sum will reach you, for these gentlemen’s word is true and beyond doubt or question.”

**37** Then Alexandria was thrown into turmoil and Cairo into agitation. The thunder of cannons rose, and the din of ranks, multitudes, and rifles broke out, so that everyone was alarmed and afraid. The unrest spread until it reached these lands. Were it not for God’s grace and mercy, the earth would have swallowed up those upon it, for, in view of the people’s heedlessness and rebellion, they deserved what befell them.

**38** In short, within a few hours Alexandria was seen turned upside down, as this mortal one has previously mentioned in some letters, and as has also been revealed by the Most Exalted Pen. The friends in Alexandria and Cairo sent a petition to the Most Holy Court asking what they should do. They also sent a petition to his honor Ismu’llāh M-H, upon him be the most resplendent of all glory, who was then staying in this land. The instruction was given that the friends of Alif and Sīn should act as circumstances required and turn toward the Most Holy Presence, while the friends in Cairo should remain where they were and be at ease.

**39** After these gentlemen arrived in the land of their desire, the heedless and treacherous set Alexandria on fire, burning or plundering people’s possessions of every kind. All the friends’ property was also plundered, and their warehouse was demolished and laid waste. In the region of Khartoum, too, the fire of war was blazing, and someone raised the banner of rebellion. Owing to the disturbances in Egypt, all those regions were in turmoil and agitation, and the honored Ḥājī ʿAbd Allāh was besieged there until the order to leave arrived. He came out, placing his trust in God, and God, exalted be His glory, preserved him from a hundred thousand calamities. Praise be to God, he reached the land of his desire and was admitted to the sacred presence.

**40** As for the gentlemen from Alexandria, although they were utterly destitute, the agent in Cairo had been dismissed, and news had arrived of the new agent’s arrival in Istanbul, nevertheless, in view of the promise that had been made, the honored Āqā Siyyid ʿAlī, may the glory of God rest upon him, sought to fulfill it. Through God’s grace and favor, a sum became available. He took it and set out for Cairo, carrying fifty British pounds, which he handed over.

**41** The believing merchants and the agent himself were greatly astonished and amazed. At first the agent refused to accept it, swearing, “I have no claim. These qualities of yours are enough for me. It is sufficient praise of you that the very people who regard you as enemies speak in your praise.” In short, this affair brought honor to the Cause in those regions. The honored Āqā Siyyid ʿAlī, may the glory of God rest upon him, has written an account of the love of the friends in Cairo such that the birds of love in the hearts of the faithful stir and take flight. Love for the sake of God truly bestows real life and brings the dead to life.

**42** Their fulfillment of this pledge is mentioned and recorded before the All-Sufficient, the Most Exalted, as a sovereign among deeds. I ask God, exalted be His glory, to confirm the friends in that land and in other lands in trustworthiness and truthfulness.

**43** The Prison Land had risen to such a station that all regions looked toward it. If any of the companions requested something from cities near or far for purposes of trade, they would hear the answer, “It is available.” Then, through the treachery of certain souls and the darkness of what was in their hearts, it fell from the first rank to the second, indeed to the third. Nevertheless, since it is the seat of the Throne, the loftiness and sublimity of the friends’ stations remain established among the people to a certain degree. Another defect has arisen in this affair: anyone who proves exceedingly malicious eventually even lays claim to divinity. God willing, may the hand of power preserve His servants and enable them to attain what He loves and approves.

**44** In every circumstance, all one’s limbs and members should proclaim the words, “There is no power or strength except through God.” At this moment I was present before the Throne, and the Desire of the unseen and the seen spoke these words: “Write to the honored ʿAlī before Akbar, upon him be My glory, My mercy, and My loving-kindness: O ʿAlī, by My command instruct My loved ones in what will exalt their stations. Say: O friends of the All-Merciful throughout the lands! Conquer the cities of hearts with the armies of deeds and character. This is what the Lord of the world has decreed upon His establishment on the Most Great Throne. Blessed is the servant who is enraptured by My call and acts according to what he has been commanded in My perspicuous Book.” End of quotation.

**45** Countless firm utterances of this kind were heard from the tongue of the Lord of creation. Blessed are those who act.

**46** Concerning what you wrote about the beloved of the heart, the honored Ḥājī Mīrzā Ḥaydar ʿAlī, may the glory of God rest upon him, and your mention of his services in the path of God: after this was presented in the Most Holy Court, these words repeatedly flowed from the tongue of grandeur: “Upon him be the glory of God. Upon him be the glory of God.”

**47** That beloved one has written the news of Māzandarān in detail. In recent days letters have arrived from every direction, mentioning his service in Q-V. After these were presented, however, for several days no command concerning this matter outwardly appeared from the Dayspring. Then, one day, these exalted words appeared from the dawning-place of the utterance of the Lord of Names—His words, exalted be His grandeur and magnified be His majesty: “O servant in attendance! If We say that it was done with wisdom, it is evident that the grunting of swine and the clamor of the ignorant have arisen. Yet if We were to consider only the clamor, We have not wished, nor do We wish, to conceal this manifest service. Therefore, from the Source of the divine command this decree proceeds: We say that he was compelled to speak and explain, and God, exalted be His glory, through His grace and favor, made him the locus and source of the exaltation of the Word. Although this exaltation caused an uproar, since he was compelled, there was and is no blame; rather, it is accepted before the Throne. We have adorned his deed with the ornament of acceptance and have mentioned him in various Tablets. Your Lord is indeed the Compassionate, the Ever-Forgiving, the Merciful, the Generous.” End of quotation.

**48** This mortal one submits that it would not be without benefit if a copy of this letter were made, corrected, and sent to various regions, for it is adorned with the verses and words of God, exalted be His glory, which truly set the world and its peoples aflame. Perhaps they will taste its sweetness and arise to do what God loves. Perhaps the fragrance of good deeds and noble character will spread abroad and awaken the heedless. The command is in His hand, and I am only a servant who turns to Him.

**49** As for the Tablets requested specifically for the friends in the land of Mīm, they were revealed in those same days, but owing to the upheavals and considerations of wisdom, their dispatch was delayed. In recent days the order has been given to send them, and, God willing, they will be sent. What that beloved of the heart wrote about them truly brought joy to the heart, and a world of love became manifest. God willing, may that beloved one and those friends at all times speak what God wills and arise to serve the Cause.

**50** Your second letter, dated the first of the blessed month of Ramadan, bestowed fresh hearing and sang a new melody of love for the Lord of oneness. After hearing and grasping it, I made my way to the station sanctified above mention and description, and, permission having been granted, presented the details. Then the Euphrates of mercy and loving-kindness flowed, and the ocean of grace surged in a manner that words cannot describe. He said—and His word is the truth:

**51** In My name, the Wronged One, the Peerless.

**52** O you who turn your gaze toward the prison, speak in praise of the Desired One, and drink of My sealed wine! Upon you be the glory of God, the All-Protecting, the Self-Subsisting. The servant in attendance has arrived with what you sent him and has presented before the Wronged One what the dove of your heart has sung in praise and remembrance of God. Blessed are your tongue and your utterance, and whoever hears your words concerning the Cause of God, the Almighty, the All-Loving. We have sent down to those brought near what, if cast upon the dust, would cause the sun of knowledge and utterance to rise from it. Thus has the Pen of the All-Merciful spoken, yet most people do not understand. You are the one who came into Our presence and saw the ocean and its waves, and the sun and its lights, and heard what He who spoke on Sinai uttered while seated upon the throne of revelation. Your Lord remembers whoever has turned to Him, spoken His praise, and arisen to serve His mighty, unassailable Cause. Do not grieve over what those who have turned toward Us are doing. By My life, had they been fair and attained recognition, they would have acted as they were commanded in various Tablets from God, the Sovereign of all creation. Thus spoke the Mother Book before, and the Preserved Tablet in this praiseworthy station.

**53** Convey to My loved ones, on My behalf, the greeting of magnification, and remind them of what will benefit and protect them and raise them to My Kingdom, which God has made the center around which all in the unseen and visible realms revolve. Say: O My friends, We counsel you to perform deeds from which the Concourse on high may perceive the fragrance of holiness. By My life, through such deeds My Cause is exalted, as are your stations beneath the domes of My care, the canopy of My glory, and the pavilion of My mercy, which has preceded all existence. Say: We are with you in every condition; We hear and see, and I am the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing. We see and conceal; We hear and remain silent. Were We to detail for you what has appeared and will appear, sorrows would seize you. Ask God, then, to transform it through a power from Himself. Your Lord is indeed the Strong, the All-Powerful. Glory and light be upon you, upon My friends, and upon those who have remained faithful to God’s covenant and pledge in this mighty, wondrous Day. End.

**54** This transient one submits to that beloved friend that, although replies to the letters are delayed, all the matters raised are subsequently revealed, one by one, from the heaven of the divine will and dispatched. Fortunately, the reason for the delay is evident, clear, and established to you. In every circumstance, forgiveness is hoped for; moreover, this transient servant feels assured concerning you, since you are informed and aware. What you wrote conveying the glad news of the arrival of the divine Tablets, the gathering of the friends and the reading of the Tablets to them, and the degrees of longing, joy, attraction, and rapture among His exalted company truly bestowed boundless happiness. God willing, may they partake in every circumstance of the sweetness of the All-Merciful’s utterance and arise to do what is fitting. How welcome is the appearance of good, pleasing deeds and qualities from those enraptured, enkindled souls! The horizons of the human world are bright and radiant with these lights. The deed of a steadfast believer is like a tree: its root is in the soil of steadfastness, its branches reach as far as God wills, and its fruits endure as long as the earthly and heavenly kingdoms. In truth, none but the Mirror of divine knowledge has reckoned, or will ever reckon, these degrees. May this blessing be yours and theirs! We ask God to grant all the people of the world a share of this goodly bounty and heavenly banquet, and not to deprive them. He is powerful over all things.

**55** Your expression of gratitude, delight, and joy for the second banquet, the newly risen sun, and the renewed bounty bestowed upon every limb a most exquisite joy—indeed, more exquisite than can be reckoned. In mentioning the renewed dawning of the divine Tablets from the horizon of grace, you wrote these words: “Furthermore, this nothingness has this time drunk so deeply and so enjoyed this supreme gift that he has found himself sovereign over all who are on earth.” After these words were presented in the most exalted, most holy court, the divine Tongue spoke these blessed words—exalted and glorified be He: “This utterance of Jinab-i ‘Ali before Akbar is like a branch of love grafted onto divine love.” End.

**56** May a hundred thousand souls, and oceans of them, be sacrificed for this blessed utterance, which has risen like the sun from the horizon of grace. Glorify your Lord with praise and be among the thankful.

**57** You wrote, in speaking of the friends of God, that they too were so enraptured by the Kawthar of the All-Merciful’s utterance that, like souls transported, they began to voice the praise of God; you also wrote denying awareness, understanding, and humanity to those among the people of the Bayan who have turned away. After this passage was presented, this perfect, authoritative utterance shone forth from the Dayspring of the utterance of divine unity. He said: “O servant in attendance! God willing, may the friends of God always be gathered together and occupied with the remembrance and praise of God. Any soul who has drunk from the Most Great Ocean will behold the world beneath his shadow. God has taught these birds to fly, and they soar above the birds of understanding and intellect. Blessed are they! Blessed are they!” End.

**58** May I be sacrificed for the one who tastes the sweetness of the utterance and beholds the suns of compassion and loving-kindness shining from the horizons of the heaven of the words of the divine Book.

**59** As to what you wrote concerning departure and consultation, that beloved friend’s presence in that land during those days was indeed necessary. It is hoped that, through His grace, God—glorified be His glory—will sanctify that blessed land from the reprehensible conduct of those among the people of the Bayan who have turned away.

**60** Glory be to God! How heedless people are! Everyone endowed with awareness and discernment is astonished at those counterfeit souls. They have enthroned ignorance in their hearts and kept knowledge and fairness outside the door. Fie upon them, upon the one who has gone astray and led them astray, and upon a calamity that walks without knowing toward whom, and that has an abyss from which the abyss itself seeks refuge!

**61** What you wrote concerning Jinab-i Aqa Mirza Lutfu’llah—upon him be the glory of God—was presented in the presence of the Lord of Eternity. This is what the Tongue of the All-Merciful uttered in the kingdom of utterance—His words, exalted be His majesty:

**62** In My name, the Counselor, the Compassionate, the All-Aware.

**63** O you who turn toward the Face! These days are the days of God. Centuries and ages cannot equal a single moment of them. An atom of this Day is seen as a sun, and its drop as an ocean. If a soul draws a single breath in the love of God and in His service, it is recorded by the Most Exalted Pen among the foremost of deeds. Were the virtues of this Day to be recounted, all would be seen struck senseless, except those whom your Lord wills. It is therefore desirable that on this Day you strive to attain the rays of the sun of God’s good pleasure. One word is better, loftier, and more enduring than a hundred thousand children. God willing, may you attain this lofty, most exalted station, so that your remembrance may endure as long as the earthly and heavenly kingdoms. Never despair in any circumstance. Cling to the hem of God’s garment and place your trust in Him. Say: “O my God, I am the one who has turned to You with my spirit, my being, my self, and all that I possess, and has laid my aspiration, my hope, my will, and my desire before the throne of Your grandeur. Through Your generosity and grace, assist me to accomplish what You have willed. You know that I have no knowledge of what benefits me or harms me. Ordain for me what is best for me. You are indeed the Witness, the Knowing, the Compassionate, the All-Knowing, the All-Wise.” End.

**64** After what you wrote concerning Jinab-i Haji Aqa—upon him be the glory of God—was presented in the Most Holy Court, this blessed Tablet descended from the heaven of the divine will. God willing, may he drink from the ocean of the All-Merciful’s utterance and be illumined by the lights of His knowledge. His words—exalted be His grandeur:

**65** He is the Most Holy, the Most Great, the All-Glorious.

**66** The light calls out, and the fire calls out. Blessed is the ear that has heard and attained what God has intended in His mighty, wondrous Day. He has come to bring life to the world, yet the peoples have sought to kill Him. Woe to them! Your Lord is indeed the Witness, the All-Aware. Say: “By God, the Mount circles around Me, and the lights have bowed down before this resplendent Light.” Among the people are those who speak out of desire, those who arise to fabricate falsehoods, and those who cling to the ones who have broken God’s covenant and His pledge. Thus has the matter been decreed, and I am among the witnesses. People of the earth, relinquish what you possess in the hope of what is with God. Thus commands you the One who speaks the truth. There is no god but Him, the All-Powerful, the Almighty. Blessed are you, for you have been mentioned in the presence of the Wronged One, and He has sent down for you what will suffice you in every world among the worlds of your Lord, if you remain steadfast. Hold fast to the Book of God and to what has been sent down from Him. Your Lord is indeed the One who strengthens, the Ever-Forgiving, the Merciful. The Scriptures have borne witness to My Book, which is this Temple that has ascended the throne despite every wayward scholar. Thus has My Most Exalted Pen spoken, as a favor from Me. Rejoice in this great favor. May the glory shining from the horizon of My kingdom rest upon those who have cast aside all but Me, held fast to My loving care, and clung to My luminous robe. End.

**67** The lights of grace have encompassed all, and the dawn of loving care has broken. A hundred thousand blessings upon those souls who have attained the Desired One today, and whom the circumstances and appearances of these numbered days have not kept from the everlasting station. The conveyance of this servant’s greetings and salutations to Jinab-i Mirza, to them, and to each of the friends of God—if possible, every morning and evening, indeed every hour, even every moment—depends upon the kindness of that beloved friend.

**68** What you had written concerning Jinab-i Rida Quli Khan—upon him be 669 \[the glory of God\]—was presented before the face of Him from whose knowledge nothing is hidden. This is what the Tongue of compassion, generosity, and grace spoke. His words—exalted be His station and great His generosity: “O Ali before Akbar, upon you be My mercy, which has preceded humankind. God, exalted be His glory, has created the entire world for the knowledge of Himself. He has desired comfort for all and has provided the means in accordance with the requirements of His wisdom. By My life, if the people of the earth were illumined by the lights of the sun of the heaven of knowledge—that is, if they held fast to what has been sent down from the most exalted horizon and the loftiest summit, and acted upon it—they would all find themselves in perfect joy, security, and comfort. What you have done for him is pleasing before the Throne. Convey greetings from the Wronged One. Say: ‘Do not grieve over what has befallen you. Something greater has befallen God. I swear by the lights of the divine countenance, this world, with all the greatness it appears to possess, has never been and is not now worthy of a single one of the friends of God. Remain steadfast in the Cause. He does what He wills and decrees what He desires.’ God willing, may he look to Him at all times and cling to His robe. He ordains for him whatever He desires, and He is the Compassionate, the Generous. Glory be upon him, patience be his, perseverance be yours, and command be Mine. I am the Ordainer, the All-Wise.” End.

**69** What you wrote concerning Jinab-i Aqa Siyyid Muhammad the physician—upon him be the glory of God—and likewise the particulars of his understanding, intelligence, devotion, accomplishments, and capacity were all presented in His presence at the seat of the Throne, at noon on Sunday in the month of Safar. This is what the Tongue of grandeur spoke. His words—exalted be His majesty: “God willing, may he receive God’s loving care, be illumined by the lights of His knowledge, drink His choice wine, and be nourished from His table. How blessed is this mighty, hallowed Day! Its fragrance has encompassed the world, and its breeze has passed over all. Blessed is the one who has been awakened by this breeze, recognized, arisen, and said, turning toward the most exalted horizon: ‘I was asleep, O my God. The breezes of Your loving care stirred me and raised me up before the horizon of Your grace. I ask You to strengthen me to serve You and to remain steadfast in Your Cause. You are powerful to do whatever You will, and within Your grasp are the reins of existence, both unseen and seen.’ O Ali, the gaze of loving care is directed toward him. Give him the glad tidings of what the Wronged One has spoken in His mighty prison. Progress has ever been and remains possible for existence in all the worlds. This is a truth beyond doubt. Glory be upon you, upon him, and upon whoever holds fast to what is right and to that through which the Cause of God, the Lord of the worlds, is exalted.” End.

**70** As to the brevity of the answer to his question sent down from the kingdom on high, that beloved friend knows that concerning these matters and stations, enough has been sent down to suffice everyone on earth. In these days, the Most Exalted Pen wishes to proclaim under all circumstances: “There is no god but Him, the All-Protecting, the Self-Subsisting.” This transitory servant asks and hopes of God, exalted be His glory, that He may strengthen him under all conditions to do whatever will exalt the Word of God.

**71** Concerning what you wrote about Aqa Khodadad and Aqa Shah-Virdi—upon them both be the glory of God—they have indeed received God’s loving care. After it was presented in the most inaccessible, most holy, most exalted Court, the Tongue of majesty spoke these lofty words. His words—exalted be His majesty:

**72** He is the Witness, the All-Hearing.

**73** O Khodadad, the Most Exalted Pen bears witness that whenever mention of you was presented, you received the divine Word and His remembrance. Ask God to enable you to recognize this noble and great station. From the time you first turned toward the most exalted horizon, a special Tablet has been sent down every day on which you have been mentioned, and beyond this, the gaze of loving care has been directed toward you. Give thanks to God, your Lord and the Lord of all who are on earth and in heaven, who has taken your hand, rescued you from the darkness of the earth, brought you beneath the shade of the Lote Tree of His loving care, and exalted your remembrance among His servants who are near to Him. His grace and mercy have ever taken precedence and continue to do so. He has delivered you, guided you to the straight path, given you pure wine to drink from the hand of His bounty, and made you one of the people of this station. Arise to serve Me, speak My praise, and hold fast to My grace, which has encompassed the horizons. End.

**74** Likewise, these radiant verses were sent down from the heaven of the will of God, exalted be His glory, concerning Jinab-i Haji Shah-Virdi—upon him be the glory of God. His words—exalted be His grandeur:

**75** In My name, the Compassionate, the Generous.

**76** O Shah-Virdi, you have attained that of which the people of the world are unaware and from which they are veiled, except those whom God wills. You journeyed, turned toward Him, and directed yourself to Him until you reached the Dawning-place of guidance and heard what the Tongue of God, the All-Powerful, the All-Knowing, the All-Wise, spoke. How many a devoted soul died longing to meet Me; how many a loving soul sought My station; how many a prince lamented separation from Me; and how many a companion gave his life to attain union with Me! You set out and resolved, placing your trust in God, until you entered a court around which the faithful Spirit circled, and heard from the Wronged One what the ears of those brought near have heard. Give thanks to God for strengthening you, bringing you near to the ocean of life, sending down for you that which nothing can equal, and causing you to hear what Moses heard. Reflect upon God’s loving care, that it may free and release you from all the circumscribed sorrows of these fleeting days. This grace calls for turning toward Him, and turning toward Him calls for freedom from sorrows. Glory be upon you and upon those who are with you. End.

**77** This transitory servant has always sought, and continues to seek, goodness, blessing, loving care, steadfastness, grace, and everlasting remembrance for these two gentlemen, whom the Most Exalted Pen has named the sons of Abraham and the heirs of Moses. Surely, at some time this prayer will be answered, for, as the Most Exalted Pen and that beloved friend testify, they have devoted and continue to devote most of their time to serving the Cause. The whole world has remembered and will remember such souls. These scattered things and varied colors will soon pass away, but what is with God will surely endure. Blessed are they! They are indeed divinely assisted. Among the signs of this assistance is that that beloved friend has expressed satisfaction with them. God willing, may they always be aided to succeed.

**78** As to Jinab-i Aqa Khodadad’s statement—upon him be 669 \[the glory of God\]—that nearly a year has passed without this servant sending a reply to what he has sent, the matter is as he has said. However, because of my confidence in him, and because mention of him flows from the Most Exalted Pen in most of the Tablets, this servant has been occupied with answering the letters of some who have newly turned toward the water’s edge. In view of his service and steadfastness in the Cause, he himself is surely content with what has occurred. God, exalted be His station, bears witness that the remembrance of him, his efforts, and his service have always been and remain before my eyes. It is hoped that, through divine grace, a reply will also be sent.

**79** As to what was written concerning Jinab-i Aqa Muhammad and Aqa ʿAli-Asghar—upon them both be the glory of God—praise be to God, they have been favored with divine remembrance both before and since. Their remembrance has indeed been sent down from the heaven of the loving care of our Lord and your Lord, our Beloved and your Beloved, and they have been inscribed by the Most Exalted Pen. This is through the grace of the One we seek and you seek. At this point these exalted words flowed from the tongue of the Sovereign of all creation and were revealed:

**80** His words, glorified and exalted is He: “O Muhammad! Blessed are you for having fulfilled your covenant, and blessed is whoever has done within it what was acceptable before the Throne. Your deed has been adorned with the ornament of acceptance in this mighty and praiseworthy station. Give thanks to God for this favor and say: ‘Praise be to You, O Sovereign of the unseen and the seen!’ We also remember ʿAli before Asghar, convey Our greetings to him, and give him the glad tidings of My mercy, which has preceded him. Blessed is he for having attained My remembrance before and since, and for having drunk My sealed wine.” End of quotation.

**81** That gentleman’s deed was most acceptable, and the deed of Jinab-i Aqa Muhammad was also favored with the ornament of acceptance. The verses of God, our Lord and the Lord of the worlds, have indeed borne witness to this.

**82** Concerning what you wrote about Jinab-i Aqa Mirza Muhammad-ʿAli and his wife—upon them both be the glory of God—after it was presented at the Most Holy Court, the waves of the ocean of divine utterance appeared and shone forth in the form of these radiant words. He said, exalted is His grandeur:

**83** In My name, the Almighty, the Magnificent.

**84** O Muhammad before ʿAli! We have heard mention of you in a letter from one who has loved Me and whom God has loved, and We have sent down for you verses that nothing in the treasuries of kings can equal. Blessed is whoever has attained today the recognition of God, at whose appearance all things declared: “The promise has come, and this is the Promised One!” We have indeed manifested the Cause, sent down the verses, and summoned everyone to God, the All-Protecting, the Self-Subsisting. Among the people are those who have cast aside guidance and embraced desire because they have followed every heedless and veiled soul. In the path of God, the Wronged One has suffered what has caused the Concourse on high and the inhabitants of the cities of names to lament; yet most of the people do not understand. Under all circumstances We arose to uphold the Cause in such a way that neither the cannons of the world nor the ranks of armies could hinder Us. The first to oppose Us were the religious scholars of the earth. They broke God’s covenant and His pledge and rose against Us, just as they had previously risen against Muhammad, the Messenger of God, and, before Him, against the Spirit. The Balance calls to them, but they do not hear; the Path warns them, but they do not perceive. They have clung to conjectures and illusions, turning away from the lights of certainty. Thus does My Most Exalted Pen recount to you in this inaccessible prison. Preserve My verses, then recite them upon the heights among the people of Baha. This is what He with whom is a preserved Book commands you. Glory be upon you and upon your wife, who has attained the choice wine of the love of her Lord, the Almighty, the All-Loving. End of quotation.

**85** O beloved of my heart! In accordance with the command, convey these mighty and exalted verses to them and deliver greetings on behalf of God, that through the breezes of the utterance of the Sovereign of all existence they may attain true joy and remain safe from the most great terror. This servant also offers them greetings and peace.

**86** Mention had been made of Jinab-i Aqa Siyyid ʿAli—upon him be the glory of God—of Kha, and likewise of his being aflame with the fire of divine love. After entering the Presence, obtaining permission, and presenting the matter, the sun of loving care shone forth in the form of these exalted words. His words, exalted is His majesty:

**87** In My name, speaking from the horizon of the Kingdom.

**88** A Tablet that the Wronged One has sent down for one who has turned toward God on a Day whose glad tidings were proclaimed beforehand by the Messengers of God and every revealed Book. O ʿAli! Call to mind what raised you up to uphold this Cause, what awakened you on this Day, and who caused you to hear the call of the Wronged One, who has witnessed in the path of God what has made those brought near to Him lament. Who informed you of this Prisoner, and who told you of this Cause, through which the rustling of the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary rose, the most exalted horizon shone, and all things spoke in the kingdom of creation? He has come who was concealed in the knowledge of God and inscribed by the Pen of the Cause in His sealed Book. Blessed are you for having heard, recognized, and turned toward Him who has come from the heaven of the Cause with manifest sovereignty. Leave the people to their desires and cling to the hem of the loving care of your Lord, the Sovereign of existence. We exhort you and those who have believed to do what will gladden the heart of the Wronged One and exalt the Cause of God, the Almighty, the All-Loving. Should He perceive the fragrance of His own character and of what He has commanded His servants in His Book, He will indeed rejoice. Thus has the Tongue of Utterance spoken in the kingdom of recognition, as a grace from Him. He is the Truth, the Knower of all hidden things. Glory be upon you, upon whoever has been set ablaze with the fire of the love of God in His days, and upon everyone who has arisen and cast aside inaction on this promised Day. Remembrance and glory also be upon whoever has awakened through the breezes of revelation that pass from the direction of My mighty and beloved prison. End of quotation.

**89** At this blessed time, verses are being revealed and clear proofs are shining forth to such a degree that a hundred thousand like this servant would truly be powerless and unable to recount, describe, record, or explain them. Grandeur belongs to God, our Lord and your Lord, the One we seek and you seek, and the One sought by all who dwell in the earthly world and the realm of power. I do not know what intoxication has seized these people. The former community used to argue that a few passages had been revealed in the Book in which God, exalted be His glory, foretold future events, and that these events had taken place; because they had occurred, they counted this as evidence and proof. Now you and all the friends bear witness that events no rational person could have imagined were revealed with complete explicitness by the Most Exalted Pen, and all, one after another, passed from potentiality into actuality and emerged from concealment into manifestation. Indeed, whatever has since appeared or may yet appear has, one after another, been mentioned in the Book and has been visibly witnessed in the outward world. Nor has this been limited, for not one, two, or three instances, but more than these and far more still, have become manifest and evident. Nevertheless, all are heedless, asleep, and dead, except those whom the hand of grace has protected. Can anyone say that in any revelation its verses have been more perfect, its clear proofs more evident, or its tree of proof more fruitful than this blessed, towering Tree? No, by my Lord—not unless he is utterly devoid of fairness. Whatever this servant has submitted or submits has been and remains veiled, for he has not had, and does not have, permission to report certain matters. God has sealed his mouth. The command is in His hand; He acts and decrees as He wills, and He is the All-Powerful, the Unconstrained.

**90** You mentioned the honored gentleman, his honor Zayn B. R., who migrated toward God and attained His presence in the Land of Mystery. God willing, may he under all circumstances receive God’s special favors and outpourings of grace. He has always been and remains before our eyes. He has never been forgotten and never will be. God willing, may he be remembered throughout all centuries and ages in association with God’s name and service to Him. At times, mention of him in particular flows from the tongue of the Sovereign of Eternity. O beloved of my heart! Beyond all other considerations, the tree of faithfulness is a blessed tree. Its fruits are cherished, and its effects and mysteries are lasting and enduring. If one considers carefully, it is the commander of the hosts of love and the leader of the people of affection and truthfulness. From the depths of my heart I offer him greetings and peace.

**91** His letter reached His Holiness the Most Great Branch of God—may my spirit, my self, and my being be sacrificed for the dust beneath His feet—and, God willing, He will graciously provide a reply. The delay in certain matters is out of wisdom. These are days when, if distinction becomes apparent, it may well cause harm—that is, to the distinguished person. Since the enemies now know with clear certainty that God, exalted be His glory, has forbidden sedition, disorder, harassment, and killing, they are somewhat restrained in certain matters; in the utmost secrecy, however, they lie in wait. If they truly recognize someone as a source of substantial influence in those regions, they resort to various devices to establish some outward fault against that person, like the fault that the cruel bird established against the helpless partridge before tearing it apart. What this transitory servant means is that, for these reasons, certain divine directives are being held in abeyance.

**92** Concerning what you wrote about the handmaid of God, Hudhud—upon her be the glory of God—on one occasion this transitory servant again made particular mention of her, and she was favored with the ornament of the loving care of God, exalted be His glory. The Tongue of Grandeur spoke these exalted words. His words, exalted is He:

**93** O you who look toward My face and arise to serve My Cause! Give her glad tidings on My behalf and convey to her My greeting of glory, at the bidding of your compassionate, generous Lord. We previously remembered her and the daughter of him who bears My name, the Most Truthful, who turned and directed himself toward God at His command, until he entered the prison, stood at the gate, and heard the call of God, the All-Powerful, the Almighty, the All-Bestowing. We bestow Our greeting of glory upon her, upon her mother, and upon My handmaids who have turned toward God, the Master of all, and We exhort them to pure deeds and whatever befits the days of God, the Lord of lords. Thus has the ocean of utterance surged as the All-Merciful walks in the highest station. End.

**94** Praise be to God, she attained what she desired. She was indeed remembered, and there was revealed for her and her daughter that through which the fragrance of our generous Lord’s loving care was diffused. The letter of that beloved of the soul concludes with a supplication to God. While it was being presented, when the reading reached these words you had written, “My God and my Beloved, honor the soul who honors Your Cause and becomes the means of exalting and elevating Your Cause,” at this point the sun of this utterance shone from the horizon of the will of the Lord of all existence. His words, exalted be His majesty:

**95** O you who drink the choice wine of My utterance! We have indeed honored you, aided you, exalted you, and remembered you, so that you may make mention of the Cause of your Lord, the Almighty, the Generous.

**96** This honor will not change, nor can the armies of the world conceal it, for God has bestowed it and it comes from God; soon its effects will appear on earth. Hold fast to My remembrance and arise to serve My Cause with joy and gladness, wisdom and utterance. Thus does the All-Merciful command you from this mighty, unassailable station. Consult with some of the friends who are sincere and trustworthy and truly adorned with love, and undertake whatever will foster unity and concord. By My life! God will exalt whoever loves Him and reveal his station among His creatures. He is indeed the protector of whoever befriends Him and the helper of whoever helps Him in His mighty, wondrous Day. End.

**97** At this point the ocean of utterance surged so mightily that this servant lost his memory, thought, and strength. We belong to God and to Him we return, and the matter is in God’s hands. I know no more. The body almost took flight—how much more the spirit! After the supplication had been presented, verses revealed, loving care expressed, mercy manifested, and grace displayed, mention of the steadfast souls who had turned toward Him—upon them be God’s glory and loving care—whose names appeared in that beloved one’s letter was presented in the most unassailable, most holy, most exalted court. This is what the Sun of Truth shone forth with from the horizon of the heaven of utterance. His words, exalted be His grandeur, great His beneficence, and immense His majesty:

**98** In My name, mentioned in the Scriptures, the Books, and the Tablets.

**99** A Book sent down from God, the Lord of eternity, to the peoples and nations. Blessed is the hearer who has heard and the discerning one who has seen, and woe to every doubting denier! O My Most Exalted Pen! Remember those who have clung to the hem of the robe of the loving care of your Lord, the Lord of Names, with a remembrance that will draw hearts and spirits to Him. Remember My servant ʿAẓīm, who acknowledged this Most Great Announcement and drank the choice wine of recognition from the hands of the bounty of your Lord, the All-Merciful, who proclaims in every circumstance, “There is indeed no God but Me, the Almighty, the All-Bestowing.”

**100** We previously remembered you from the direction of the White Spot, from the Tree beyond which there is no passing, with a remembrance from which the fragrance of eternity spread among the peoples. Thank God for this most great remembrance in My Most Great Prison, and say, “Praise be to You, O Dawning-Place of revelation and Revealer of verses!” By My life! All the treasures of the earth cannot equal a single letter of My verses. To this bears witness He with whom is the Mother Book.

**101** Say: O peoples! By God, the Book speaks at the pivot of the world and summons the nations to the Lord of eternity, yet the people are sunk in an astonishing sleep. Say: He has come before whom all the books of the earth have bowed. Take heed, you who have insight! Be mindful of the All-Merciful, O inhabitants of the realm of existence! Judge fairly this Cause, at whose appearance the trumpet was sounded and the mountains passed away. Say: O peoples of the earth, bring what you possess, and We will weigh what We possess and what you possess in this Balance, which has been established with justice at the command of God, the Lord of lords. This is a day when the Balance calls out at the top of its voice, “I am indeed the discerning, the all-knowing, from the Lord of religions.”

**102** We also remember him who is named Ḥaydar from this Most Great Outlook, that it may gladden him with My mercy and loving care and draw him near to a station that God has made the place around which the highest Paradise and the inhabitants of the Kingdom of Names circle at evening and at dawn. By My life! Were you to learn what is with your Lord, joy and gladness would seize you in a manner that pens are powerless to describe. Arise to serve My Cause, speak My praise, look toward My horizon, and cling to the hem of the robe of My loving care. Thus have We commanded you before and in this Tablet, from whose horizon the sun of wisdom and utterance has shone. O Ḥaydar! Exhort My servants to adopt My character and follow what has been sent down in My Book. Your Lord is indeed the Ordainer, the Almighty, the All-Knowing. Beware lest the affairs of creation keep you from the True One. Set aside all but Me, then turn your face toward Me and say, “I bear witness that You were inscribed by the Most Exalted Pen and concealed in the knowledge of God, the Master of all.” Praise God that you were mentioned in the presence of the Wronged One and that there was sent down for you that through which the horizons were illumined.

**103** O ʿAlī, whose name precedes Akbar! Upon you be My glory and My mercy. Rejoice that the Most Great Ocean has turned toward you from this most luminous, most ancient station and has wished to remember your paternal uncle and his son, that they may rejoice in the remembrance of God on a day when faces have darkened and feet have slipped. Blessed is the receptive one who has heard and turned toward Him; woe to the one who has turned away from Him whom he remembered by night and day! We give them both glad tidings and bestow upon them Our greeting of glory from this station, that they may arise to serve My Cause, before which all necks have bowed. We also remember God’s loved ones and His friends in the lands of Sīn and Nūn, and gladden them with the sun and its radiance, the ocean and its waves, the heaven and its loftiness, the stars and their lights, and what has been inscribed for them by My Most Exalted Pen in the Crimson Scroll. Thus does God reward His servants as a grace from Him, and He is the Almighty, the All-Bountiful.

**104** O Yaḥyā! Listen to the call from the direction of ʿAkkā, from the Tree on the right side of the luminous Spot: “There is indeed no God but Me, the Self-Sufficient, the Most Exalted.” Do you recognize Him who causes you to speak, and do you know who has turned toward you? Say: “Yes, by Your own Self! He who spoke on Sinai speaks to me, and the Lord of Revelation has turned His face toward me as a grace from Him. He is in truth the Self-Sufficient, while I am poor and needy.” O Yaḥyā! Exhort My servants to trustworthiness and truthfulness and to whatever will exalt the remembrance of God in cities and lands. Conquer hearts with the hosts of good character. Thus have We commanded the servants before and in this Book. Thus have We adorned the brocade of the Book of Existence with the remembrance of the Desired One, that you may thank your Lord, the Lord of humankind.

**105** We also remember him who is named Mawlā in this most exalted station with My sweetest call, and I have power over whatever I will. Arise in remembrance and praise, and glorify your Lord, the Lord of the place of return. We have remembered you with a remembrance through which the valley has flowed and the sweet waters of My mercy have streamed from every direction. Say: O people! Do not deprive yourselves of the ocean of life. Be mindful of the All-Merciful, who has come with the hosts of revelation and the banners of verses. Say: Will what you see today remain yours? No, by My own Self, the True One! Those on earth will perish, and sovereignty will remain His alone. To this every tree, stone, clod, and pebble bears witness.

**106** We also remember Hādī, whom We guided to the straight path. O Hādī! The Wronged One remembers you and enjoins you and those who have believed to do what is right. Follow what you have been commanded by the Cleaver of the dawn. By God! The Day of God speaks the truth in this palace, which God has made the Most Great Outlook. Recognize this, you who possess understanding! Say: Set aside what the people possess; the Sovereign of existence has come with the banners of revelation and inspiration. O peoples of the earth! Be mindful of God, and do not deprive yourselves of Him through whom what was concealed in the Books and Tablets has been revealed. Take hold of the Book of God with strength, and do not follow any ignorant doubter. Thus have We illumined the horizon of the heaven of recognition with the light of utterance. Blessed is whoever has heard and seen, and woe to every heedless schemer!

**107** O My Most Exalted Pen! Remember the one who heard your rustling and turned toward you, who is named Yūsuf, so that he may rejoice in this remembrance, before which all remembrances bowed down when it appeared. We have appeared and manifested the Cause in such a way that hearts were shaken and eyes stared in astonishment, except those who cast vain imaginings behind them and turned toward God, the Dawning-Place of lights. Blessed is whoever has attained to hearing My call, perceived the fragrance of My robe, and awakened through the breezes of My loving care as they wafted at dawn. This is a day when all things have been enraptured by the call of the Lord of Names, yet the people remain heedless and asleep. Blessed is whoever has perceived the fragrance of utterance and arisen to serve the Cause morning and evening. We heard your remembrance and remembered you; We saw your turning toward Us and turned toward you from the Dawning-Place of remembrances.

**108** We also remember ʿAlī before Muḥammad, and give him and those who have believed in that place the good news of My mercy, My loving care, and My grace, to which the atoms have borne witness. In all matters, place your trust in Him who spoke on Sinai, and hold fast to what has been sent down in the Book by the Sender of the winds. Beware lest the vain imaginings of the learned keep you from the Creator of heaven, or the might of rulers frighten you away from the Dawning-Place of certitude. Pay no heed to these few days: they will pass, and those who affirm God's unity will see themselves in the loftiest gardens of paradise. We enjoin you to exercise wisdom under all circumstances, lest the clamor of those who have denied the ultimate return arise. Thus has the fragrance of utterance spread throughout existence. Blessed is whoever has perceived it, and woe to every scheming denier!

**109** We also remember My loved ones in Shīn and Hāʾ, give them the good news that I have turned toward them, and greet their faces with words of glorification from this station, which is adorned with the lights of the face of their Lord, the Almighty, the Ever-Forgiving. O My loved ones! Rejoice in what has been sent down for you from the heaven of the Cause, and thank your Lord, the All-Merciful, at all times. He has forgiven you, guided you, and favored you above most of His servants. We have remembered everyone whose name was mentioned before Our face, as well as those whose names were not mentioned. He does as He wills through a sovereignty of His own, and He is the All-Powerful, the Almighty, the All-Knowing.

**110** We also remember the one named Khānlar and give him the good news of My inexhaustible favors. Rejoice that We have remembered you and those who have believed in verses for which souls would be sacrificed. Confine your affairs to the remembrance and praise of God. Whenever one of His loved ones comes to you, arise to serve him with joy and gladness. Beware lest the affairs of this world and what happens in it grieve you. Leave it behind you and hold fast to the cord of God, the Lord of creation. Glory rest upon you, your sons, your family, and everyone who is assured and steadfastly patient. End.

**111** After the waves of the ocean of meanings and the manifestations of the lights of divine utterance, what can this servant mention, and what can he present? On one occasion, these exalted words issued from the tongue of the Lord of Names. Truly, the heart is set aflame by them, sighs ascend, and tears fall. His words—exalted be His grandeur:

**112** “O servant in attendance! You see and hear how, night and day, the rustling of the Pen of grace rises and the call of the Wronged One rings out, all for the guidance of the servants and the salvation of those on earth. If only, in return for this supreme gift and this immense compassion, they would unite in the Cause of God and hold fast to whatever brings about its elevation and exaltation, so that a sweet fragrance might spread from pure deeds and spiritual qualities and acquaint the world with what has appeared. If this fragrance rises, it is a truthful envoy and a perfect messenger who makes things clear. Blessed is whoever has attained to My utterance and recognized what the kingdom of My will has intended.” End.

**113** This poor one remains bewildered and astonished at what has appeared. They turn toward the buzzing of a spider and turn away from the rustling of the Most Exalted Pen. They cherish a foul odor and are deprived of the fragrance of the most exalted Paradise. All matters are manifest and evident. You will see it; thus has He who possesses the Mother Book informed me.

**114** At this moment, your third handwritten letter passed over this dry, prostrate body like the breeze of the true spring, bestowing gifts and showing kindness. Praise be to God, the herald of love continues to appear and pass by. God willing, this herald will not be hindered or cease to move.

**115** After reading it and acquainting myself with its contents, I turned toward the peerless station. After entering the presence and receiving permission, the prayer of that dear friend was presented with the utmost joy and gladness before the throne of the All-Merciful. This is what the Tongue of Eternity and Lord of the world spoke. His words—blessed and exalted is He:

**116** “O you who turn toward My face and are enraptured by My verses! We have heard your call and what you whispered in prayer to God, your Lord. We have heard your sighs and seen your tears in your love for God, your Beloved and your Goal. We have witnessed the fire of your love, the burning of your heart, your submissiveness and humility, and the trembling of your limbs in love and affection for God. We were with you in gatherings and assemblies when you spoke of this Most Great Name and this Announcement of which We gave the prophets and messengers glad tidings. Blessed are you and those whom vain imaginings have not held back, who arose and said, ‘God is our Lord and the Lord of the mighty throne.’ Greet My loved ones on My behalf with words of glorification. Say: By God! My heart laments and My eyes weep at what has befallen My mighty and wondrous Cause. Hold fast to the cord of unity and to what you have missed in the days of God, the Lord of the worlds. Thus have We kindled the lamp of counsel with the oil of grace and the fire of love. If you will not protect it from the winds, do not be the cause of its extinction. Be mindful of the All-Merciful, and reflect on the loving care of your Lord, the Ever-Forgiving, the Merciful. Arise to serve the Cause: it is better for you than all that has been created in the heavens and the earths.” End.

**117** With a hundred thousand tongues, this ephemeral servant beseeches the friends of God to cry out from their souls and strive together, so that the people of the world may become informed and aware of what God—exalted be His glory—has intended. If they reckon up the dissension and perceive unworthy deeds, by the life of my Beloved and yours, they will flee and scoff. In one of the Tablets He says that the friends must be like a pulsating artery in the body of the world. Therefore, all must manifest such deeds and qualities that the whole world will thereby turn toward Him and be stirred into action. May a hundred thousand lives be sacrificed for those who act for God! Where are the souls who put God before themselves and do in His path what brings about the advancement and love of the world's people? Through God's grace, there is hope that the seeds of loving care deposited in hearts will sprout and become adorned with exquisite fruits. The matter is in His hand, and He is the Strong, the All-Powerful.

**118** Your pen had made mention of the honored Āqā Shaykh ʿAbbās, upon whom be the glory of God. This matter was presented before the throne of the Dawning-Place of the light of divine unity, and this most exalted Tablet was sent down especially for him from the heaven of loving care. God willing, he will drink from the Euphrates flowing in the divine Tablet and attain the reward of the Presence and the favor of our Lord, the Lord of Names. His words—mighty be His utterance, exalted His grace, and great His grandeur:

**119** He is the Witness, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.

**120** O ʿAbbās! The Wronged One remembers you with a remembrance through which those brought near are drawn toward God, the All-Protecting, the Self-Subsisting. The Hour has come, the call has risen, the cry has sounded, and the mountains have passed away, yet the people are unaware. The world has been overturned, the throne has been established, and the Lord of Revelation, who spoke on Sinai, has seated Himself upon it, yet most people do not understand. The Mother Book has appeared and calls out between earth and heaven with the loudest call, summoning everyone to the praised station. Among the people are those who have denied, those who have turned away, those who have disputed the verses of God, the Lord of all that has been and will be, and those who have broken God's covenant and His pledge with an injustice that has caused the inhabitants of the cities of names and the dwellers of the Kingdom to lament. When We looked discerningly, We found that most of Our enemies were the learned. Thus does the Tongue of the All-Glorious recount to you from the most exalted horizon. He is indeed the Truth, the Knower of things unseen.

**121** We brought forth knowledge so that the One who is its object might be recognized. Yet when the horizon of revelation shone and that One came, the learned denied Him at the very outset, except those whom God, the Master of existence, willed otherwise. Say: O company of the learned! Set aside what you possess. By God, the sound of the Most Exalted Pen has risen, announcing to all the appearance of the One toward whom you turned every evening and morning. Say: Why do I see you, O company of the heedless, making your way to the House while turning away from Him who raised it by a command from Himself? Fear God and do not follow your desires. Rather, follow Him who has come to you with a manifest Book, before which, when it appeared, all the books of the world bowed down. Be fair, O people, and do not be among those who have denied the witness and the witnessed. This is the Day promised to you in the scrolls of God and His books, and this is the Cause whose covenant was taken by Him who possesses the knowledge of all that has been and will be.

**122** Say: O company of the unjust! You have done what has caused the Concourse on High to cry out, the people of Paradise to lament, the sighs of the highest heaven to ascend, and the tears of the angels and the Spirit to fall. Say: If you possess anything greater than what has come from the dominion of the divine Will, bring it forth, and do not follow every ignorant outcast. Say: Come, that I may show you what you have overlooked in this Day that has been attributed to God, the Almighty, the All-Loving. This is a Day in which the fragrance of the All-Merciful has spread abroad, the breezes of revelation have wafted, and the Nightingale of the Cause has spoken upon the branches: “Sovereignty belongs to God, the King of kings.”

**123** O ʿAbbās! Arise to serve the Cause in the name of your Lord, the Master of eternity, and remind the people of this Most Great Announcement, whose appearance has made the limbs of vain imaginings and idle suppositions tremble. Beware lest the power of rulers and the doubts raised by the learned keep you from the Master of names. Be as a firmly rooted mountain in this irrevocable Cause. Say: He has come in truth and pays no heed to your acceptance or rejection. He has appeared and brought forth whatever He wished, despite you, if you only knew. He is the One who declares in every circumstance: “There is no God but Me, the Single, the One, the Almighty, the Beloved.”

**124** Thus We have opened before you the door of grace with the key of justice. When you attain it, say: “Praise be to You, O God of the unseen and the seen! I bear witness that You have cast aside comfort for the advancement of the nations, accepted abasement for the exaltation of the world, and chosen exile so that Your servants might reach the most exalted homeland, the station that God has sanctified beyond the grasp of minds.” O you who have turned toward the Face! Take the sealed wine in the name of the Wronged One, then drink from it with this remembrance through which souls and hearts have been drawn in rapture. With My Most Exalted Pen We have inscribed for you the reward of attaining Our presence upon the Crimson Scroll. Rejoice, then give thanks to the Lord of the Frequented House. We have accepted your turning toward Us, your devotion, and your work in the path of God. Blessed are you, for your deeds have been adorned with the ornament of acceptance. End.

**125** O beloved of my heart! It is as though a herald stands upon every word of the divine utterances, calling at the top of his voice to all who exist. Glory be to God!
